chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Dawud ibn Sulayman al-Kufi, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said:

A man from my household fell ill, so I went to visit him as a sick-visitor. I said to him, 'O son of my brother! I have a piece of advice for you — will you accept it?' He said, 'Yes.' So I said, 'Say: I testify that there is no god except Allah, Alone, with no associate for Him.' So he testified to that. I said, 'This will not benefit you unless it comes from you with firm conviction.' So he affirmed that it was from him with conviction.

Then I said, 'Say: I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.' So he testified to that. I said, 'This will not benefit you until it comes from you with firm conviction.' So he affirmed that it was from him with conviction.

Then I said, 'Say: I testify that Ali is his successor, and he is the Caliph after him, and the Imam of obligatory obedience after him.' So he testified to that. I said to him, 'You will never benefit from that until it comes from you with firm conviction.' So he affirmed that it was from him with conviction. Then I named the Imams one by one, and he acknowledged each and affirmed that he was upon conviction.

It was not long before the man died, and his family grieved over him with intense grief. He (the narrator) said: I was absent from them, then came back to them after that and found them in good condition. I said, 'How do you find yourselves? How is your composure, O woman?' She said, 'By Allah! We were struck by a great calamity with the death of so-and-so — may Allah have mercy on him — but what consoled my heart was a dream I saw last night.' I said, 'And what was that dream?' She said, 'I saw so-and-so — meaning the deceased — alive and well.' I said, '(Are you) So-and-so?' He said, 'Yes.' I said to him, 'Had you not died?' He said, 'Yes, but I was saved by the words that Abu Bakr had instilled in me, and had it not been for that, I would nearly have been destroyed.'

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ: Ashhadu — I testify/bear witness; the standard formula of the shahada
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ الْمُفْتَرَضُ الطَّاعَةِ: The Imam of obligatory obedience — a technical Shia creedal formulation identifying the divinely appointed Imam whose obedience is binding
key_terms.تَلْقِين: Talqeen — the Islamic practice of instructing or prompting the dying or deceased with the articles of faith
key_terms.وَصِيّ: Wasiyy — executor, legatee, successor; used here as a title for Ali ibn Abi Talib
key_terms.يَقِين: Yaqin — absolute certainty, firm conviction; a condition stipulated for the benefit of the testimony

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia practice of talqeen (indoctrination) at the time of death?
ai.summary: Abu Bakr al-Hadrami narrates that he visited a dying relative and administered the talqeen — instructing him to confess the shahada (divine unity and prophetic mission) and then explicitly the imamate of Ali and all twelve Imams, each time emphasizing that conviction (yaqin) was essential for it to benefit him. After the man died, his widow reported a dream in which the deceased appeared alive and said that the words Abu Bakr had taught him were what saved him from destruction. This narration powerfully illustrates the Shia doctrine that confessing the imamate with conviction at the time of death is salvific, and that the talqeen rite is an act of mercy for the dying believer.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
